title: 1M Events/sec Streaming Distinct-Count & Top-K Without OOM
prompt: Your real-time telemetry pipeline ingests 1,000,000 events/sec across 16 Kafka/Flink worker pods (4 GB RAM per pod) and tracks 50,000,000 unique `user_id`s and `endpoint`s per 1-hour sliding window across 200 tenants. Using per-pod `HashSet` and `HashMap` aggregations causes pods to exceed 12 GB and crash with `OOMKilled` (exit code 137) within 10 minutes, while shuffling raw `user_id`s across nodes saturates the network. Design a <1 MB/shard streaming analytics architecture.

spark.summary: Replace per-pod HashSets and HashMaps with 16 KB HyperLogLog sketches (for distinct users) and 256 KB Count-Min Sketch + size-K Min-Heaps (for Top-K endpoints), merged across workers in 1-minute tumbling sub-windows.
spark.keyTakeaway: When a single bottleneck threatens end-to-end availability, decompose 1-hour sliding windows into sixty 1-minute tumbling HLL + CMS sketches so workers merge fixed kilobyte arrays in <1 MB RAM.
spark.byteSummary:
Tracking 50M distinct `user_id` strings in an in-memory `HashSet` across 200 tenants and 1-hour sliding windows blows past 4 GB pod limits in minutes (`OOMKilled` exit code 137). Even if pods had 64 GB RAM, shipping raw sets across the network to compute global cluster-wide `COUNT(DISTINCT)` saturates NICs.

The bounded-memory architecture replaces exact sets/maps with two mergeable sketches per `(tenant, 1-minute pane)`: a **HyperLogLog** (`p=14`, 16 KB) for `+-0.81%` distinct `user_id` counts, and a **Count-Min Sketch** (`d=5, w=12,800`, ~256 KB) paired with a **size-100 Min-Heap** for Top-K `endpoint` heavy hitters.

To support a **1-hour sliding window** without storing raw events, maintain a ring buffer of **60 one-minute tumbling panes** per tenant (`60 * 16 KB = 960 KB` for HLL, or ~16 MB total across panes if kept on-heap / offloaded to RocksDB state). Each minute, workers emit only the closed 1-minute sketch (~270 KB) to the aggregator, which merges across all 16 workers (`max` for HLL, `sum` for CMS) and slides the 60-pane window.

The core trade-off is ~0.8%–1% cardinality error and ~0.1% frequency error in exchange for deterministic, OOM-proof memory and 100x less cross-node network traffic—while supporting an optional exact-count fast path for low-cardinality (<1,000) tenants.

learningJourney.title: Handling Tenant Skew & High-Volume DDoS Bursts
learningJourney.purpose: Prevent one massive tenant from polluting smaller tenants' Count-Min estimates.

explanation.foundation: If Tenant A generates 900K events/sec (`N_total = 54M/min`) while Tenant B generates 100 events/sec, a **single shared CMS** has error `epsilon * N_total = 0.001 * 54M = 54,000`—swamping Tenant B's true count of 100!
explanation.core:
- **Isolate Whale Tenants**: Route heavy-hitter tenants (`> 10K events/sec`) to dedicated per-tenant CMS instances, while small tenants share a pooled CMS (or use exact `dict` until cardinality > 1,000).
- **Exact-to-Sketch Promotion**: Start new/small tenants in a tiny 1,000-entry `dict` and promote to HLL+CMS only when `len > 1,000`.
